instruction.text: Some kinds of storms are very different to the ones we get in the UK. Find the sand cloud to learn more.

feedback.end: This is a sandstorm. Sandstorms are caused by big storms passing over deserts and lifting sand into the air. We don’t have any sandy deserts in the UK, so we don’t get this kind of storm.

instruction.text: Find the storm in this image to learn more.

feedback.end: This is a tornado. Tornadoes are towers of air that spin around very quickly. Some are so powerful that they can rip apart houses! Tornados are never very big or dangerous in the UK.

instruction.text: Some storms get much bigger than the ones we have in the UK. Find and select the water on the ground to learn more.

text: This is a hurricane. Hurricanes are very large, spinning storms that form over the ocean. They are so big that they can be seen from space!

instruction.text: Match the definitions to the correct type of extreme weather.

atoms.b: a tower of air that spins around very quickly
a very large, spinning storm that forms over the ocean
a storm over a sandy desert that pulls sand into the air

instruction.text: What do you think is the safest thing to do during a sandstorm, tornado, or hurricane? Select the correct option.

feedback.correct: Correct! During all of these types of extreme weather, you should seek shelter in a building to protect yourself.
feedback.wrong1: It’s always good to stay positive, but now might not be the best time for a party!
feedback.wrong2: Getting away from the storm is a good idea, but all of these storms can travel much faster than you can run!
